headline: Sensex and Nifty end lower as surging oil prices and geopolitical tensions snap two-week winning streak

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Crude oil prices surged to near six-month highs of $114 per barrel due to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia triggered a fourth consecutive day of selling in Indian equities
Dr Reddy’s reported a disappointing 36% year-on-year decline in Q2 net profit
Infosys cut its FY27 revenue guidance despite securing a $5.2 billion deal bonanza
whatHappening: The Nifty 50 ended at 22,600, while the Sensex fell 126 points after crashing 1,250 points from its intraday high
Market breadth weakened significantly with only 15% of midcap stocks trading above their 50-day moving average
Petronet LNG and Gruner Renewable formed a joint venture to invest ₹1,200 crore in compressed biogas plants
Havells India expects festive season demand to support growth and improve margins for its Lloyd brand
summary: Indian benchmarks snapped a two-week winning streak as surging crude oil prices and West Asia tensions weighed on investor sentiment. Corporate earnings added to the pressure, with Dr Reddy's reporting a sharp profit fall and Infosys lowering its long-term guidance. Despite the broad market decline, stocks like Petronet LNG and Havells saw positive momentum from strategic deals and festive outlooks.
